items.stem: A researcher randomly selects 3 soil samples from a collection of 15 samples consisting of 4 acidic samples, 5 neutral samples, and 6 alkaline samples. What is the probability that exactly 1 selected sample is acidic and at least 1 selected sample is neutral?
items.explanation: The total number of selections is C(15,3) = 455. Favorable selections contain 1 acidic sample and either 2 neutral samples or 1 neutral and 1 alkaline sample, so there are C(4,1)[C(5,2) + C(5,1)C(6,1)] = 160; the probability is 160/455 = 32/91.

items.stem:
I. P(A and B)=0
II. P(A or B)=11/20
III. P(neither A nor B)=9/20
items.stimulus: A randomly selected day at a laboratory is classified as either a day on which Machine A requires maintenance, a day on which Machine B requires maintenance, or neither. The events A and B are mutually exclusive. If P(A)=3/10 and P(B)=1/4, which of the following statements must be true?
items.explanation: Mutually exclusive events cannot occur simultaneously, so P(A and B)=0. Since A and B cannot overlap, P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)=3/10+1/4=11/20. The probability that neither occurs is 1-11/20=9/20. Therefore, all 3 statements must be true.

items.stem: A laboratory reading is incorrectly recorded with probability 1/8 on each trial. The trials are independent, and a report is accepted only if all 3 readings are correct. What is the probability that a report is accepted?
items.explanation: The probability that 1 reading is correct is 1 - 1/8 = 7/8. Because all 3 independent readings must be correct, the probability is (7/8)^3 = 343/512.

items.explanation: Because B can occur only when A occurs, event B is contained within event A. Therefore, the probability of both events is P(B) = 0.43, and the probability of at least one event is P(A) = 0.74, so statement II is false. The probability of A without B is 0.74 - 0.43 = 0.31, making statements I and III true.
